business_process: Emergency alarm call-out, H2S monitoring, and release reporting
description: SCADA alarm call-out of H2S, tank high-level, pump station, and shutdown events to on-call staff; spill and release reporting
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Local hardwired shutdowns and beacons work without SCADA, but nobody is told remotely; an oil discharge that reaches water must be reported to the National Response Center immediately (40 CFR 110.6); roving patrols can stand in for about 4 hours before crews are exhausted
manual_workaround: Roving patrols of sour-gas sites every 2 hours; Production Controllers phone field crews; spill reports by phone from the HSE on-call binder
dependent_third_parties: Cellular carrier; radio tower leases; microwave link provider
dependent_people_or_facilities: Production Controllers; Field Superintendents; HSE on-call; OCC and BCC
quantified_operational_impact: About 60 sour-gas sites in the Panhandle and Alabama need patrols; 14 extra crew members per shift
quantified_regulatory_impact: Immediate NRC notice for any discharge reaching water; state spill notices per the emergency response plan
safety_environment_impact: Severe: H2S exposure to staff or neighbors, or an unreported release
part195_linkage: Yes: the call-out also carries gathering pump station and trunk line pressure alarms used to detect a release (BP-04)

description: 3 water injection plants and 24 saltwater disposal wells take about 340,000 barrels of produced water per day; SCADA monitors pressures and rates against permit limits
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Water storage at tank batteries and plants fills in about 8 hours at full rate; then producing wells must be shut in; injection pressure limits are permit conditions
manual_workaround: Plant operators run each injection plant from its local PLC panel; shut in the highest-water-cut wells first
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-02 (plant PLCs; disposal well RTUs); SYS-08
quantified_operational_impact: 340,000 barrels of water per day; storage covers about 8 hours; each hour past MTD shuts in about 4% of production
quantified_regulatory_impact: Injection pressure above permit limits is a state permit violation
safety_environment_impact: Moderate: overflow or overpressure risk if plants are left unattended

description: 24x7 OCC monitoring of 640 wells and 24 facilities; remote start and stop; pump-off control and ESP drive settings
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Without SCADA every site must be visited by truck; crews can cover the Panhandle and Alabama radio sites for about a day; the 180 cellular sites (mostly South Florida) are shut in after 24 hours
manual_workaround: Manual operations: lease operators run routes, gauge tanks by hand, and shut in wells they cannot cover; Field Superintendents set the shut-in order
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-02; SYS-08; SYS-05 (OT directory sync)
dependent_third_parties: SCADA integrator; cellular carrier; radio tower leases
dependent_people_or_facilities: Production Controllers; lease operators; automation technicians
quantified_operational_impact: About 15% of production is lost while running manually (about $99,000 per day) plus about $60,000 per day of overtime and contract crews
quantified_regulatory_impact: Production reports to the state can be completed late from field records
safety_environment_impact: Moderate: degraded visibility of pressures and levels
part195_linkage: Indirect: the OCC also runs the gathering system (BP-04)

business_process: Gathering system operation and pipeline safety monitoring
description: Remote operation of the gathering pump station and trunk line valves; pressure and flow monitoring of the 92-mile gathering system; leak analytics (AI-003)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Company pipeline procedure: if SCADA pressure and flow monitoring of the regulated trunk line is lost and the pump station cannot be staffed within 8 hours, the trunk line is shut down; Panhandle tank batteries then hold about 2 days of production before wells are shut in
manual_workaround: Station operator on site runs the pump station from its local panel; line riders patrol the regulated 14-mile trunk line every 4 hours; hardwired high-pressure shutdown switches protect MOP
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-02 (pump station PLC; LACT flow computers); SYS-08; SYS-14
dependent_third_parties: Third-party transmission pipeline (receipt point); 5 shippers; electric utility
dependent_people_or_facilities: Production Controllers; gathering operators; Pipeline Compliance Manager
quantified_operational_impact: Panhandle crude (5,600 barrels per day, about $375,000 per day) depends on the gathering system after the 2-day storage buffer; shipper volumes about 1,400 barrels per day
quantified_regulatory_impact: An accident on the regulated line needs NRC telephone notice within 1 hour of confirmed discovery (49 CFR 195.52) and a written report within 30 days (195.54); reporting-regulated lines need the written report (195.15)
safety_environment_impact: Severe: an undetected release near a drinking water unusually sensitive area
part195_linkage: Yes: 195.11 regulated rural gathering line (14 miles) and 195.15 reporting-regulated lines (78 miles)

business_process: Custody transfer measurement and shipper volume statements
description: 6 LACT units with flow computers at the Panhandle Central Facility; meter proving; daily shipper volume statements on the shipper portal; monthly gathering invoices
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Flow computers keep their own audit records, so measurement continues; Central Facility and battery storage give about 2 days before Panhandle wells shut in if LACT units cannot run; shippers rely on daily statements for their own nominations
manual_workaround: Paper tickets from flow computer front panels; manual proving records; statements by email from the Measurement Supervisor
dependent_systems: SYS-02 (LACT flow computers); SYS-14; SYS-04 (OT data account; shipper portal); SYS-05
dependent_third_parties: Third-party transmission pipeline; 5 shippers; flow computer vendor
quantified_operational_impact: About 7,000 barrels per day pass the LACT units; each day without statements adds about 30 manual tickets and shipper reconciliation work
quantified_regulatory_impact: Measurement disputes under the gathering agreements; no federal deadline
part195_linkage: Indirect: LACT units are at the delivery end of the gathering system

business_process: Truck custody transfer: tank gauging and run tickets
description: Tank gauging, run tickets, and loading of purchaser trucks at 8 tank batteries; run tickets entered in the field data capture app
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Tank storage holds about 3 days of production; if trucks cannot load, wells are shut in; run tickets are the basis for sales and royalties
manual_workaround: Paper run tickets signed by the gauger and the truck driver; tank strapping tables in the tank battery binders
dependent_systems: SYS-04 (field data capture app); SYS-09 (tablets); SYS-03
dependent_third_parties: Crude purchasers and their trucking carriers
quantified_operational_impact: About 4,200 barrels per day leave by about 25 truckloads; paper tickets add about 2 hours of rework per 10 tickets
quantified_regulatory_impact: None directly; state production reports rely on these volumes

description: 4 compression stations deliver associated gas to third-party gas gathering systems through lease sales meters
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Station PLCs run locally; without compression, wells making associated gas must be curtailed within about a day
manual_workaround: Station operators run compressors from local panels; curtail high gas-oil-ratio wells
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-02 (station PLCs; flow meters); SYS-12 (packager gateways)
dependent_third_parties: Gas gathering companies; compressor packager; electric utility
quantified_operational_impact: Curtailing high gas-oil-ratio wells defers about 600 barrels of oil per day in addition to the gas
quantified_regulatory_impact: Flaring limits under state rules if gas cannot be delivered
safety_environment_impact: Moderate: emergency shutdown events at stations

business_process: Production allocation and state production reporting
description: Daily volume allocation from run tickets, LACT tickets, and meter data; monthly close; state production reports in Florida and Alabama
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Month-end close and state reports have fixed due dates; allocations can be rebuilt from tickets and meter data
manual_workaround: Rebuild daily volumes from paper tickets and flow computer printouts
quantified_operational_impact: About 32 staff; each day of outage adds about 2 days of rework at month end
part195_linkage: Indirect: volumes feed the Part 195 annual report (195.49)

business_process: Royalty and revenue distribution and joint interest billing
description: Monthly payments to about 14,000 royalty owners; joint interest billing to 22 non-operating partners
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Royalty payments go out monthly and owners notice late payments; partners pay their share of costs from the monthly billing
manual_workaround: Delay the payment run and notify owners; issue partner billings from the prior month's template
quantified_operational_impact: About $14 million of royalty payments and about $9 million of partner billings move each month; a 5-day delay generates about 1,500 owner calls
quantified_regulatory_impact: State law on late royalty payment may apply in each state (counsel confirms)

description: Work orders, rig and crew scheduling, parts; predictive maintenance alerts (AI-001)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About 5 pump failures a day across 420 producing wells; each failed well waits for a rig; a 3-day backlog is manageable with whiteboard scheduling
manual_workaround: Whiteboard rig schedule at each field office; paper work orders; phone dispatch
dependent_third_parties: ERP vendor; parts suppliers; data science firm
quantified_operational_impact: Each day of delay defers about 600 barrels of production from wells waiting on rigs

description: Segment identification, MOP, operator qualification, damage prevention, and public awareness records; accident and annual reports
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Records must be available to regulators and kept for the periods in 195.11(d); the 1-hour accident notice is by telephone and does not depend on systems
manual_workaround: Printed MOP and emergency contact sheets at the OCC and pump station; OQ cards carried by qualified staff
dependent_third_parties: Pipeline records software vendor (in the productivity suite)
quantified_operational_impact: About 120 OQ records and 14 miles of segment records
quantified_regulatory_impact: Missing records would be an enforcement finding under the record retention duty (195.11(d))

business_process: Treasury, payables, and crude sales settlement
description: Accounts payable, purchaser and transmission pipeline statements, bank reconciliations, credit facility reporting
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Purchasers pay monthly; vendors tolerate a short delay; the borrowing base certificate is quarterly
manual_workaround: Manual payments for urgent payables with call-back verification; statements by email
quantified_regulatory_impact: Covenant reporting dates under the credit agreement (contract)

description: Biweekly payroll for 850 employees; time capture from field crews; onboarding and terminations
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll runs biweekly; missed payroll has legal and retention impact
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll through the payroll provider; paper time sheets
quantified_operational_impact: 850 employees paid biweekly; about 600 field time sheets per cycle
quantified_regulatory_impact: Wage payment timing rules in each state

description: Seismic interpretation, reservoir models, and waterflood surveillance for drilling and injection decisions
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: No daily operation depends on it; the risk is confidentiality (trade secret), not downtime
manual_workaround: Defer analysis; work from local copies

description: Dispatch of 70 company drivers hauling produced water and fluids; haul tickets; vehicle telematics for location and hours
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: South Florida disposal depends partly on trucked water; driver hours rules need records
manual_workaround: Radio and phone dispatch; paper haul tickets and logs
quantified_operational_impact: About 160 loads a day; manual dispatch cuts loads by about 20%
quantified_regulatory_impact: Driver records of duty status must be kept by other means

description: Email, files, chat, and the enterprise AI assistant used by all office staff
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Most coordination with partners, shippers, and regulators runs through email; out-of-band phones cover incidents
manual_workaround: Company phones, text groups, and printed contact lists
